terms.comment: A plain description: to lack a living (quaestus, see employment), as Plautus describes the poor, quibus nec quaestus est (Rud. 2.1.2). The unemployed are quī quaestū carent.

Egger’s phrase: freedom from work that is not wanted. Ōtiōsus, which Lewis & Short glosses “unemployed”, means at leisure or without public office, a condition a Roman chose, so it does not say out of work.

phrases.latin: pauperēs hominēs, quibus nec quaestus est
phrases.english: poor men, who have no living

phrases.latin: Frāter ejus jam sex mēnsēs quaestū caret.
phrases.english: His brother has been out of work for six months now.

sources: Lewis & Short: quaestus · Lewis & Short: careo · Lewis & Short: vacatio · Lewis & Short: otiosus
